title: Orchestrate deterministic streaming scenarios and isolate CPU/GPU contention tests
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: Our perf regression and load test suites have increasing flakiness and noisy variance driven by two root causes: non-deterministic RNG/seeding across distributed runners, and cross-tenant CPU/GPU contention in shared CI nodes. This causes spurious regressions, long investigation cycles, and low confidence in canary rollouts.

Goal: Introduce a deterministic, data-driven streaming scenario layer and runner-level isolation knobs so the perf harness produces reproducible results in CI and when run on dedicated infra. Deliverables: (1) Scenario schema v2 that encodes stream event timing, prefix caching toggles, and seed vectors; (2) Runner isolation flags (cpu-set, gpu-mem-limits, cgroups wrapper) and a lightweight node-allocator for CI; (3) Cross-run seeding protocol that derives per-run RNG from a global seed plus stable run id; (4) CI gating job to fail on non-deterministic variance above thresholds and capture deterministic replay artifacts.

Why now: Related refactors (plugin registry and runner protocol) made it possible to introduce migration step without breaking existing tests. Reducing flakiness will speed up perf triage and decrease false positive rollbacks.

Non-goals: This work does not change model kernels or quantization logic. It also does not attempt to solve noisy hardware-level thermal throttling beyond providing reproducible isolation configurations and recommended instance types.
acceptance_criteria: Scenario schema v2 implemented and documented in the harness README
All existing streaming scenarios ported with preserved semantics and a migration script
Per-run deterministic seeding demonstrated: five repeated runs on identical input produce token-level identical traces (or within documented divergence points)
Runner isolation flags exercised in CI with at least two instance types (cpu-only and GPU) and variance thresholds enforced
A CI job (perf/determinism) fails when variance exceeds threshold and uploads replay artifacts to the perf-dashboard S3 path
PRs merged and a follow-up smoke against dedicated infra shows 30% reduction in flaky perf alerts compared to baseline
comments: 2026-03-05 - Priya Shah: Created the ticket after multiple flake incidents in last three weeks. Linked initial incident notes and dashboard queries.

2026-03-06 - Jordan Kim: Did an exploratory run on a local k8s single-node. Found RNG inconsistencies: different Python runner processes were re-seeding from time.time() in one plugin. Marked that plugin for immediate fix (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/462).

2026-03-08 - Engineering review: Decision to implement seed derivation scheme <global-seed>::<runner-id> and to centralize seed propagation in the runner bootstrap. Trade-off: small backward incompatibility for third-party plugins that rely on implicit randomness; we'll add a compatibility shim for 2 cycles.

2026-03-09 - Design review (SRE & CI): Opted for lightweight cgroup-based isolation tooling (run-isolate) over full VM reprovisioning to keep CI minutes reasonable. We will provide recommended instance classes for noise-sensitive tests.

2026-03-10 - Jordan Kim: Implemented runner flags and added 'isolate=true' to the local runner. Basic smoke is green. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/475. Requesting PM/QA review for migration plan.

2026-03-11 - Priya Shah: Added migration task to docs and created a small dataset with deterministic seeds for the most common streaming scenarios. Uploaded examples: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PerfDeterminismExamples
